title: Elision Comparison Workbench
description: Teaching comparison of three ways to hide a field and keep the proof on one synthetic shipment record. Panel 2 applies SD-JWT salted-hash disclosures (the T545 approach): an elided claim leaves only its unrecoverable _sd digest. Panel 3 applies the estate's sha256-salted@1 commitments: every field is an opaque commitment, the salt stays with the committer. Panel 4 builds an Envelope-style digest tree per IETF draft-mcnally-envelope-12 sections 4.1 to 4.4: eliding a node keeps its digest, so the root digest over the whole record is unchanged. Panel 5 shows why the draft salts: an unsalted elided digest over a guessable counterparty is recovered by a corpus attack while a salted one is not. Illustrates the draft; not a conformant Envelope implementation.

record.description: Synthetic shipment record to commit to.

elide.description: Field to elide from the shared record.

mcp_tool_definition.name: compare_elision_commitments
mcp_tool_definition.description: Teaching demo: elides one field of a synthetic shipment record and compares what an SD-JWT verifier, a sha256-salted@1 verifier, and an Envelope-style digest tree verifier still see. Shows the root digest is unchanged by elision and that an unsalted elided digest over a guessable value is recoverable while a salted one is not. Illustrates draft-mcnally-envelope; not a conformant Envelope implementation.
